headline: My Application Form for the Competitive Exam Is Currently Serving as a Table Mat at the Testing Agency’s Cafeteria
body:
I didn't expect my dreams of a government job to end on a sticky Formica table in the testing agency’s canteen, but there it was: my admit card, complete with my photo and exam roll number, being used to prevent a spilled cup of ginger tea from staining the wood. I had walked into the headquarters to inquire about my missing results, only to find the staff using a stack of student registration forms as makeshift trays for their samosas.

When I politely asked a clerk about the status of my application, he didn't even look up from his lunch. He simply pointed to the 'official filing system'—a pile of forms precariously balanced next to a large plastic jar of salty biscuits. It appears my future isn't being 'processed' by algorithms or experts, but is instead being slowly laminated by the condensation from a glass of buttermilk.

I’ve tried to reclaim my documents, but the office manager insisted that my application has been 'reallocated to the internal culinary department' for the foreseeable future. Apparently, they found the high-GSM paper I printed it on to be remarkably absorbent. As I stood there, watching a senior official casually set his hot lunch plate down on a pile of answer sheets, I realized that the parliamentary panel’s concerns about the agency's arrogance might be a bit understated. They aren't just ignoring our data; they are actively repurposing it to keep their office tea parties leak-free.
caption: When the government asks for your credentials, they mean for you to literally serve them. #NTA #TestingAgency #ExamStress #Bureaucracy (satire)

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 excels because it uses a highly specific, grounded domestic image—the exam admit card as a tea coaster—to illustrate institutional dysfunction. It manages to feel like a sympathetic, relatable observation of bureaucratic absurdity rather than a cynical takedown, maintaining a high level of structural fidelity and a punchy, deadpan tone throughout.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses satire to critique bureaucratic inefficiency and systemic mismanagement at testing agencies. It does not name any real individuals, targets an abstract institution rather than a specific religious or ethnic group, and maintains a whimsical tone that is clearly satirical rather than defamatory.
